explanation: When designing concurrent systems where multiple worker tasks must wait for a single initiating event (a 'broadcast' pattern), standard `std::future` is insufficient because it is designed for a single consumer and transfers ownership of the shared state upon retrieval or waiting. Solution: `std::shared_future`. By obtaining a `std::shared_future` via `std::future::share()`, the resulting future object allows any number of threads/tasks to safely wait on the same shared state simultaneously. This is the primary mechanism for synchronizing the simultaneous start or completion of multiple consumers based on a single producer signal.
keywords: std::shared_future, future share, concurrent broadcast, one-to-many synchronization
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
